Former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is joining the artificial intelligence company OpenAI in a national security-related role, the organization announced on Monday.

"Dan Driscoll will join OpenAI as Senior Counselor for National Security Modernization, working with senior leadership and external partners to advise on how advanced AI can strengthen national and cybersecurity, with a particular focus on working with U.S. allies to advance its responsible use," the organization noted.

"In this newly created role, Dan will work with OpenAI teams and leaders across governments, industry, academia and allied institutions to advance practical modernization initiatives that support the buildout of democratic AI. He will also help internal OpenAI teams understand the operational needs of global national security institutions."

THIS ROBOT DOG WAS MADE TO SAVE SOLDIERS' LIVES AS US RACES INTO NEW ERA OF AUTONOMOUS WARFARE

U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll speaks during a House Armed Services Committee hearing on Capitol Hill May 15, 2026 in Washington, D.C. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images / Getty Images)

Driscoll, who became Army secretary last year under the Trump administration, departed the military post in September 2026.

Driscoll also served as acting director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) during parts of 2025 and 2026. His service in the two posts overlapped for a period of time earlier this year.

MARVELL, LUMENTUM TOUT HISTORIC $115B DEAL TO CREATE ‘CATEGORY LEADER’ IN AI CONNECTIVITY

Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and President Donald Trump attend a dignified transfer at Dover Air Force Base for military casualties of the war with Iran on July 22, 2026, in Dover, Del. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images / Getty Images)

"I’ve spent much of my career in public service, first as a Soldier and most recently as Secretary of the Army and Acting Director of ATF," Driscoll said in the OpenAI announcement.

"The people who serve deserve the very best tools we can put in their hands. National security requirements are changing faster than at any time in the past fifty years. This technology will help them keep pace by cutting through paperwork, making sense of more information, and getting the right answer to the right person faster.

"I’m joining OpenAI to help the United States and our allies put this technology to work responsibly, for the people who keep us safe."

ANTHROPIC, OPENAI CEOS WARN AI COULD THREATEN HUMANITY WITHOUT SAFEGUARDS

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman speaks during OpenAI DevDay in San Francisco Sept. 29, 2026. (Minh Connors/Bloomberg via Getty Images / Getty Images)

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said, "AI should give people more power over their lives, and people should have a say in how it’s developed. The U.S. has an extraordinary opportunity to work with other countries to spread the adoption of democratic AI, and I’m excited to welcome Dan Driscoll to OpenAI to strengthen American leadership and help us do that."
